title: Hybrid continuous batcher: length segmentation + KV GC policy
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts followed by long responses and vice versa) cause inefficient continuous-batcher slot utilization and KV cache fragmentation, increasing GPU memory pressure and latency variance. Goal: implement a hybrid continuous batching approach that segments incoming requests by expected token-length band and introduces a lightweight KV garbage-collection (GC) policy that reclaims cold KV entries while preserving hot conversational prefixes. This ticket covers design, experiments, implementation proof-of-concept, and initial rollout on a canary fleet.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end hybrid batcher implemented and gated behind feature flag
Observed 12%+ reduction in 95th percentile per-request latency for mixed-length trace in canary compared to baseline
GPU memory fragmentation metric reduced by at least 18% for canary workloads
KV cache hit rate for conversational prefixes remains within 3% of baseline for high-volume customers
Automated regression tests for correctness and a smoke suite for canary rollout documented
design_notes: Use lightweight length estimator upstream: sample first 8 tokens of prompt to predict remainder using linear model derived from historical traces
Create 3 dynamic length bands: SHORT (<64 tokens), MEDIUM (64-512), LONG (>512). Bands can be tuned via runtime config
Maintain separate batching queues per band with configurable max-slot latency thresholds and cross-band opportunistic coalescing if slot idle > threshold

KV GC policy: two-tier TTL + LRU hybrid. Short-lived prefixes (TTL 15m) set for one-off prompts; long-lived conversational prefixes pinned with access counter and only evicted when global KV pressure > watermark
KV shard annotations tracked in memory to avoid full-scan during GC; GC operates incrementally per GPU epoch to limit jitter
Preserve API semantics: responses must be stable; ensure KV reclamation does not break ongoing requests by marking entries 'draining' before deletion
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (3d): Instrument length estimator and create banded queues in the scheduler (feature-flagged)
Phase 2 (4d): Implement opportunistic coalescing and per-band slot thresholds; add metrics emission for per-band latency and slot utilization
Phase 3 (5d): Implement KV GC controller with TTL and pinned-entry logic; add shard annotations and incremental GC loop
Phase 4 (3d): End-to-end integration tests and canary rollout to 5% of serving capacity
Phase 5 (2d): Analyze canary metrics, adjust thresholds, and prepare gradual ramp if targets met
metrics: GPU memory fragmentation index (bytes free holes / total GPU memory)
KV cache hit rate for pinned prefixes vs ephemeral prefixes
Batch slot utilization and bytes-per-batch token
GC pause time per GPU epoch
Error rate and unexpected OOM occurrences
test_plan: Unit tests for length estimator accuracy on sampled historical traces
Integration test simulating mixed-length trace (short prompt -> long response bursts) and asserting latency and GC invariants
Chaos test: trigger KV pressure artificially and assert pinned prefixes are preserved and 'draining' semantics hold
Performance regression harness against canary dataset with statistical significance tests
E2E smoke tests for API correctness while GC is active
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: start with non-customer-facing internal canary (10% requests) for 48h
If no regressions and target metrics met, extend to 5% customer-facing fleet for 72h
Monitor dashboards and automated alerts for latency, OOMs, and KV eviction spikes; rollback if p95 increases >5% or OOMs observed
Gradual ramp to 50% over a week with daily reviews, then full release gated by runtime-1.24 cut
risks: Estimator misclassification causing long responses forced into short-band leading to timeouts or poor tail latency
KV GC incorrectly evicting hot prefixes causing quality regressions for multi-turn agents
Increased scheduler complexity may introduce scheduling bugs and deadlocks if cross-band coalescing is not carefully synchronized
Instrumentation overhead from per-band metrics could slightly increase CPU usage
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha: Created ticket after spike showing frequent OOMs during morning traffic on mixed-dialog workloads. Attached profiler traces and sample traces.
2026-03-03 Luca: Prototype of length estimator implemented. Quick A/B shows 86% classification accuracy on recent trace sample. Low-cost: uses first-token heuristics plus historical percentiles.
2026-03-05 Engineering: Implemented separate band queues behind feature flag. Initial microbench shows p95 latency improvement for SHORT band but MEDIUM band sees slight regression under load.
2026-03-08 Design review: Decided to add 'draining' state for KV entries to avoid deleting entries referenced by in-flight requests. Design doc updated: Confluence link in artifacts.
2026-03-10 QA: Added integration tests for GC draining semantics. Found race condition when coalescer moved a request between bands while GC marked entry for drainage — fix scheduled.
2026-03-12 Luca: Fixed race by adding lightweight request pin to KV controller and tuned opportunistic coalescing threshold from 20ms -> 35ms. Ready for internal canary rollout.
